_readme: The DDCS Studio header wordmark, DECLARED. brand/trace-wordmark.py is a DUMB INTERPRETER of this file — it holds no font/size/colour/shear constants of its own. Every mark is two lines: the 'DDCS' wordmark and the 'CNC MACRO STUDIO' tagline, each made of one or more coloured LAYERS (a layer = one traced line of text, offset/coloured/filtered independently — a mark with a bevel or a glow just stacks more than one layer of the same text). Regenerate a mark by re-running trace-wordmark.py against this file; never hand-edit a MARK-*-TRACED.svg's path data directly.
traps: SHEAR SIGN IS NEGATIVE: sh = -tan(radians(slantDeg)). The y-flip in scale(s*xscale, -s) runs BEFORE the shear in the transform chain, so a positive shear leans the letters the WRONG way. Assert it: transform a point at cap height (e.g. y=700 in font units) and confirm the resulting x-delta from the baseline point is POSITIVE (leans right). This shipped wrong once.

GOOGLE FONTS WOFF2 FETCH: the URL must carry '&text=DDCS%20CNC%20MACRO%20STUDIO' (every glyph either line uses) AND a MODERN User-Agent string. An old/absent UA gets EOT instead of WOFF2; omitting &text= gets a Cyrillic subset with no 'D' in it at all. Both actually happened. The response's font url does NOT reliably end in '.woff2' either — a live Sniglet response came back as a '/l/font?kit=...' endpoint with no file extension at all; match any fonts.gstatic.com url(), don't require a literal suffix (t2163, also actually happened).
SYSTEM FONTS (normal/studio/futuristic/steampunk) load from %WINDIR%/Fonts/ariblk.ttf, arialbd.ttf, georgiab.ttf directly via fontTools — no fetch, no &text= concern.

'fit':'targetWidth' layers (the four AS-IS marks) compute xscale PER RUN as targetWidth / naturalWidthAtSize — always re-derive it from the live glyph metrics, never hard-code a captured xscale number for these; the font file is the source of truth.
'fit':'blend' layers (organic only) use a DECLARED xscale + trackingEm instead of a full fit-to-width stretch — see the organic mark's own note for why.
PRECISION: round path coordinates to 1 decimal on output (0.1 unit on a 150-unit box = 0.07% error, visually identical, ~66% smaller file than full float).

SNIGLET EXTRABOLD (wght 800) IS NOT USABLE — historical, kept for anyone tempted to try Sniglet again (t2161, root-caused t2163, upstream-confirmed t2165): its 'D' glyph's inner counter is a genuine ~79x79-unit fragment against a ~610x723-unit outer contour (under 13% of the width) — a real defect in the published outline data, not an extraction bug. Confirmed identical in the Google Fonts API copy AND github.com/google/fonts' own canonical OFL source (byte-identical contours — rules out a serving-pipeline artifact). Sniglet REGULAR (wght 400) does NOT have this defect (~61%-width counter) but is too light a weight to stand beside the other four marks. organic now uses Fredoka Bold (700) instead — see marks.organic below and brand/README.md. If Sniglet's publisher ever fixes weight 800's 'D', that is the only thing that would make revisiting it worthwhile; nothing in this declaration or trace-wordmark.py needs to change to try it again, only the organic entry's font{}.

studio.note: the engraved-nameplate bevel: each line is stamped TWICE, a light layer offset +dx/+dy behind a dark layer at the true position, same font/size/slant/fit both times.

organic.status: SHIPPED (t2165) as Fredoka Bold (700), not Sniglet. Sniglet ExtraBold's own 'D' is broken upstream (confirmed against github.com/google/fonts' canonical OFL source — byte-identical contours to the Google Fonts API copy, so it is not a serving-pipeline artifact), and Sniglet Regular (400) is too light to stand beside the other four marks — so per the advisor's own call the face swapped to Fredoka Bold, the runner-up from the original live-specimen comparison. Vendored from its upstream OFL source (brand/fonts/) rather than fetched live, since it ships as a variable font pinned at a fixed instance. D/C/S all verified with correctly-proportioned counters/openings by rendering standalone and reading the letters — installed in index.html.
organic.note: human's ORIGINAL choice was Sniglet; this entry targets Fredoka Bold as the fallback after Sniglet's own upstream defect (see the traps entry). 9deg shear KEPT (a family-lean constant — matches futuristic/normal, independent of which rounded face fills this slot). 'fit':'targetWidth' (plain fit-to-width, the same treatment the four AS-IS marks use) was used rather than re-deriving a bespoke blend/tracking ratio like Sniglet's own 68/32 — that blend was a judgment call specific to Sniglet's particularly round bowls; Fredoka's plain stretch (~2.26x wordmark, ~1.84x tagline) rendered legibly and correctly-proportioned on inspection, so no new blend parameter was invented. If a future look decides Fredoka reads too stretched, a blend is the next thing to try — it was not ruled out, just not needed to ship a correct mark.

sniglet400Candidate.status: SPECIMEN ONLY (t2167) — NOT SHIPPED, NOT INSTALLED in index.html. The human, seeing the Sniglet 800 D-glyph comparison, asked to trace Sniglet 400 too — the one Sniglet weight whose 'D' is intact (confirmed t2163/t2165: ~61%-width counter, correct). This entry exists to PRODUCE that comparison specimen through the same declared path as every real mark (this file + trace-wordmark.py, unmodified), not to propose shipping it. Fredoka Bold remains the organic mark that ships until the human says otherwise. Same slot treatment as marks.organic (size/baseline/slant/fit/colours) so the ONLY variable between this and the shipped mark is the font — a fair like-for-like comparison, not a differently-tuned specimen.
sniglet400Candidate.note: t2167's own incidental proof: if this traces with a correct, properly-proportioned 'D' counter through the IDENTICAL pipeline that produced Sniglet 800's broken one, that is independent confirmation the extraction code was never the fault — the defect is specific to the 800 weight's own published outline, not this script, not fontTools, not the transform kernel. Expected to read visually LIGHT next to the four Arial-Black-derived marks (normal/studio/futuristic/steampunk) and Fredoka Bold — that weight mismatch is the actual question the human is evaluating, not a defect in this trace.

sniglet800Candidate.status: SPECIMEN ONLY (t2167) — NOT SHIPPED, NOT INSTALLED. The broken weight, traced through the exact same declared path as sniglet400Candidate (identical size/baseline/slant/fit/colours, only the weight differs), so the two can be compared as true like-for-like specimens — both went through the identical trace-wordmark.py kernel (shear, scale-to-width, 1-decimal rounding), not raw untraced font outlines. This is what a human visual request (t2167, mid-turn) asked to see directly: the actual traced 'D', not an approximation of it.
sniglet800Candidate.note: Expected to reproduce the same broken counter t2161/t2163/t2165 already found and root-caused — this entry exists to let that be SEEN through the real pipeline output, not re-litigated.
